corrections: If a turn must be continued for area orientation, stop the roll, pause momentarily to allow Number 2 to adjust, then begin the roll smoothly back into the turn.
Use the mirrors, if necessary, and communicate with the other crewmember when required to assist monitoring Number 2; be ready to take evasive action and/or direct a breakout.
As a technique, trim for a slower airspeed can help make a smooth vertical pull up.
Should a breakout become necessary, use flight controls, power and speed brake as the situation dictates; break out in the direction that most quickly ensures separation.
Consider environmental conditions such as sun angle and cloud layers, and plan formation manoeuvring to avoid them.
sections.notes: Table 9.2 (T-6 WW Ex Training Levels and Parameters) is embedded as a graphic on PDF page 236 and its cell values could not be extracted from the text layer; only the prose parameters above are captured. Note under Table 9.2: "Depending from the wingman's proficiency ET Exercise can be initiated from Level II or Level III." A leaf of the Level 3 WW Ex is a vertical pull-up with both an apex and bottom of a lazy eight-type manoeuvre.

sections.title: PRACTICE LOST WINGMAN PROCEDURES
sections.technique_summary: Lost wingman procedures are practiced in VMC only, to prepare for actual lost wingman situations in IMC. Number 1 directs the practice with a radio call; Number 2 acknowledges but does not begin execution - the acknowledgement simply verifies that Number 2 knows the exercise has been directed. Number 1 is primarily responsible for flight path deconfliction while Number 2 is heads down during the procedure.

parameters.name: meteorological condition for practice
parameters.verbatim: Lost wingman procedures are practiced in VMC (only) to prepare for actual lost wingman situations in IMC.

procedure_steps: Number 1 directs: "Mistras A2, go practice lost wingman".
Number 2 acknowledges "2" but does not begin execution.
When ready, Number 2 executes the appropriate lost wingman procedure and makes the appropriate radio call ("Mistras A1 roll out, Mistras A2, lost wingman").
Number 1 monitors Number 2 to ensure adequate separation is maintained.
Number 2 ends the exercise by conveying "visual" with a radio call; Number 1 then directs a rejoin or other position.
common_errors: Beginning execution on acknowledgement instead of when ready.
corrections: Number 1 may issue a reference heading when practicing straight and level lost wingman procedures; it is common for Number 2 to apply the procedure and then turn to that reference heading before calling visual.

sections.title: BREAKOUT PROCEDURES (PRACTICE)
sections.technique_summary: Breakouts are practiced in VMC only and are normally directed by Number 1 during practice, though during an actual breakout either A/C may initiate. After the initiating call, all manoeuvring and radio calls are identical to an actual breakout. The priorities are: ensure safe separation, establish appropriate communications, and get the formation back together.

parameters.name: meteorological condition for practice
parameters.verbatim: Breakouts are practiced in VMC (only).

parameters.name: breakout priorities
parameters.verbatim: The priorities are: a. Ensure safe separation, b. Establish appropriate communications c. Get the formation back together.

procedure_steps: With Number 2 in sight, either A/C initiates with a radio call: "Mistras A2 break out" (Number 1 initiating) or "Mistras A2 is breaking out" (Number 2 initiating).
Number 2 calls "Mistras A2 is breaking out" and executes the appropriate breakout manoeuvre.
After separation is established, Number 1 calls "Roll out".
Number 2 calls "Visual".
common_errors: Number 2 obtaining excessive range during the breakout.
corrections: If Number 2 appears to be obtaining excessive range, Number 1 may direct Number 2 to roll out with a radio call; Number 2 acknowledges, rolls out, obtains and calls "visual" with Number 1, and awaits further direction.

sections.title: CLOSE TRAIL EXERCISE
sections.technique_summary: Close trail practices manoeuvring with Number 2 in a position below and behind Number 1, with Number 1 manoeuvring similarly to the wing work exercise. Close trail spacing is one to two A/C lengths (nose to tail) behind Number 1, just below Number 1's wake turbulence and prop wash. Number 2 maintains position primarily with power, anticipating power changes as Number 1 manoeuvres.

parameters.name: close trail spacing
parameters.value: one to two A/C lengths nose to tail
parameters.verbatim: Close trail spacing is one to two A/C lengths (nose to tail) behind Number 1, just below Number 1's wake turbulence and prop wash.

parameters.name: two ship lengths reference
parameters.value: elevator tips line up about one-third of the way out the wings
parameters.verbatim: At approximately two ship lengths, the tips of Number 1's elevator line up about one-third of the way out the wings (just past the dihedral break in the wing).

parameters.name: vertical reference
parameters.value: engine exhaust stacks visible directly on top of the wing
parameters.verbatim: As a vertical reference, the engine exhaust stacks should be visible directly on top of the wing.

parameters.name: manoeuvring limitations
parameters.verbatim: Close trail maneuvering limitations are the same as wing work exercise.

procedure_steps: Number 1 directs close trail with a radio call ("Mistras A2, go close trail") or visual signal, from close (fingertip), route or echelon, and waits for Number 2 to call in before manoeuvring.
Number 2 acknowledges by the same means used to direct, manoeuvres into position (typically manoeuvring as in the cross under) and calls "Mistras A2 is in".
Number 2 maintains position primarily with power, anticipating power changes; during turns at higher G, small amounts of lead or lag pursuit may be necessary.
Number 1 manoeuvres smoothly and predictably using combinations of turns and lazy eight type manoeuvres and maintains positive G at all times.

Reform: Number 1 directs close (fingertip) with a shallow wing rock or radio call; Number 2 goes to the left side if Number 1 is wings-level, or to the inside of the turn if Number 1 is turning, unless directed otherwise.
common_errors: Flying high in the close trail position - "To prevent encountering wake turbulence, never fly high in the close trail position."
Any space between the engine exhaust stacks and the wing means Number 2 is too high and the possibility of encountering wake turbulence increases.
Attempting to correct excessive spacing forward with power alone - "If excessive spacing develops, do not attempt to correct forward with power alone."
Number 1 making sudden releases of back stick pressure, rapid or inconsistent turn rates, or rapid turn reversals.
Number 1 manoeuvring before Number 2 calls in.
Closure rates are difficult to recognize and correct for when directly behind and below Number 1.
corrections: Add power and establish a small amount of lead pursuit if in a turn; if wings-level, move off to one side to obtain a better visual perspective of Number 1's A/C.
The two most important points are to remain below Number 1's wake turbulence and always keep Number 1 in sight.
Number 1 manoeuvres smoothly and predictably and avoids significant power changes until Number 2 is in the directed formation position.
Another technique is to make a "T" out of the aft edge of the speed brake and the UHF/VHF antenna.

sections.title: PITCHOUT
sections.technique_summary: A pitchout provides spacing for rejoin practice: normally a level, 180 degree turn performed sequentially by the members of a formation. Number 1 clears in the direction of the desired turn and begins a turn away from Number 2 using approximately 60 degrees of bank and sufficient G to establish the desired airspeed. Number 2 stays visual, delays 2 to 3 seconds or as briefed, then turns to follow.

parameters.name: Number 1 bank
parameters.verbatim: begin a turn away from Number 2, using approximately 60 of bank and sufficient G to establish the desired airspeed

parameters.name: turn amount
parameters.verbatim: Normally fly a level turn of about 180.

parameters.name: Number 2 delay - standard
parameters.value: 2 to 3 seconds, giving approximately 500 to 1000 feet of separation at roll out
parameters.verbatim: Delay 2 to 3 seconds or as briefed, which should provide approximately 500 to 1000 feet of separation at roll out

parameters.name: Number 2 delay - extended
parameters.value: 5 to 7 seconds, giving approximately 1500-2000 foot spacing
parameters.verbatim: A 5 to 7 second delay will result in approximately 1500-2000 foot spacing.

parameters.name: spacing adjustment point
parameters.verbatim: After approximately 90 of turn, vary bank and back stick pressure to attain desired spacing

parameters.name: roll out position
parameters.value: behind and slightly below Number 1, 1-2 ship widths above the horizon
parameters.verbatim: roll out behind and slightly below Number 1. Place Number 1 approximately 1-2 ship widths above the horizon.

procedure_steps: Number 1 directs a pitchout with a visual signal or radio call and clears in the direction of the desired turn.
Number 1 begins a turn away from Number 2 using approximately 60 degrees of bank and sufficient G to establish the desired airspeed, normally a level 180 degree turn.
Number 2 stays visual, delays 2 to 3 seconds or as briefed, then turns to follow Number 1.
After approximately 90 degrees of turn, Number 2 varies bank and back stick pressure to attain the desired spacing and rolls out behind and slightly below Number 1.
Number 2 calls "ready" when at the desired range and rejoins when directed.
Number 1 allows enough time for Number 2 to complete the pitchout and directs the rejoin after hearing Number 2 call "ready".
common_errors: Sacrificing clearing to maintain precise altitude control or an exact 180 degree turn - "Do not sacrifice clearing to maintain precise altitude control or an exact 180 turn."
corrections: Slight climbs or descents are acceptable for energy management; the degrees of turn may be adjusted for weather, area orientation and/or energy management.

sections.title: TAKE SPACING
sections.technique_summary: Take spacing sends Number 2 to a trail position when a pitchout is not practical. Number 1 directs with a radio call ("Mistras A2 take spacing") or visual signal. Spacing can be achieved with a combination of manoeuvre and deceleration by Number 2 and/or acceleration by Number 1. At the desired range, Number 2 calls "ready"; Number 1 then slows to the rejoin airspeed and directs a rejoin.
procedure_steps: Number 1 directs Number 2 to take spacing with a radio call or visual signal.
Number 2 reduces power and/or uses speed brake to slow and increase spacing; one technique is for Number 1 to accelerate.
At the desired range, Number 2 calls "ready".
Number 1 slows to the rejoin airspeed and directs a rejoin.
corrections: Another technique is for Number 2 to take spacing by performing a series of "S" turns behind and below Number 1's prop wash.

sections.title: RANGE ESTIMATION (MIL-SIZING)
sections.technique_summary: Range to an object can be determined if the size of the object is known. One mil equals one foot at 1000 feet; for the T-6 this gives specific apparent sizes measured at 20 inches from the pilot's eye. Cockpit tools used to compare A/C size include the AOA indexer, the FCP canopy bow mirrors and the anti-collision strobe light flash guard on the leading edge of the wingtip.

parameters.name: mil definition
parameters.value: one mil equals one foot at 1000 feet
parameters.verbatim: One mil equals one foot at 1000 feet.

parameters.name: measuring distance from eye
parameters.verbatim: this equates to the following A/C dimensions when measured at 20 inches from the pilot's eye

parameters.name: T-6 apparent size at 300 feet
parameters.verbatim: At 300 feet, a T-6 is approximately 111 mils or 5.6 cm (2.2 inches).

parameters.name: T-6 apparent size at 500 feet
parameters.verbatim: At 500 feet, a T-6 is approximately 67 mils or 3.4 cm (1.3 inches).

parameters.name: T-6 apparent size at 1000 feet
parameters.verbatim: At 1000 feet, a T-6 is approximately 33 mils or 1.7 cm (0.7 inches).

parameters.name: 300 feet cues
parameters.value: width of AOA indexer turned sideways or 3/4 mirror width
parameters.verbatim: Width of AOA indexer turned sideways or mirror width. Detail visible (canopy details, pilots). Tail flash easily readable (letters, not numbers).

parameters.name: 500 feet cues
parameters.value: 1/2 mirror width; A/C size twice the wingtip anti-collision strobe flash guard
parameters.verbatim: mirror width. A/C size approximates twice the size of the wingtip anti-collision strobe flash guard. Normal fingertip references apparent.

parameters.name: 1000 feet cues
parameters.value: narrow width of AOA indexer or 1/4 mirror width; A/C size approximates the strobe flash guard
parameters.verbatim: Narrow width of AOA indexer or mirror width. A/C size approximates the size of the wingtip anti-collision strobe flash guard. A/C detail lost. Tail flash not visible.

procedure_steps: Compare the apparent size of the other A/C against the AOA indexer, canopy bow mirrors, or the wingtip anti-collision strobe flash guard.

Cross-check with detail cues: at 300 feet canopy details and pilots are visible and the tail flash letters are easily readable; at 500 feet normal fingertip references are apparent and tail letters are visible but not clearly readable; at 1000 feet A/C detail is lost and the tail flash is not visible.
sections.notes: Table 9.3 (Range Estimation) values are captured above; the fraction glyphs for mirror width (3/4, 1/2, 1/4) are partially lost in the source text layer.

sections.title: EXTENDED TRAIL (ET) - GENERAL, LIMITS AND ENTRY
sections.technique_summary: Extended trail uses lead, lag and pure pursuit options and lift vector placement to practice three-dimensional manoeuvring in relation to another A/C, flown from the fighting wing position. Number 1 provides a stable platform with consistent, predictable roll rate and no sudden changes in back-stick pressure; Number 2 manoeuvres within the fighting wing cone through proper pursuit curve and lift vector application with a fixed power setting. Both A/C initially set and maintain the same power setting.

parameters.name: the bubble
parameters.value: 300 foot spherical safety buffer around each A/C
parameters.verbatim: The 300 foot bubble is a safety of flight limit that surrounds each A/C. If an A/C is inside the 300-foot bubble during ET call "knock it off."

parameters.name: ET manoeuvre limit
parameters.verbatim: The Extended Trail (ET) maneuver limit is a 500 foot slant range. Momentary deviations within 500 feet are acceptable if it is quickly recognized and remedied.

parameters.name: minimum airspeed Over The Top
parameters.verbatim: Minimum airspeed for Over The Top is 100 KIAS.

parameters.name: torque roll conditions
parameters.value: greater than 60 % torque with high AOA (stick shaker) and less than approximately 40 KIAS
parameters.verbatim: High power settings (greater than 60 % torque), combined with high AOA (stick shaker), and slow airspeed (less than approximately 40 KIAS), can result in an unintentional torque roll.

parameters.name: ET entry energy
parameters.value: 180 to 200 KIAS, approximately the middle of the altitude block
parameters.verbatim: At an appropriate energy level (180 to 200 KIAS and approximately the middle of the altitude block), Number 1 directs the ET with a radio call

parameters.name: ET entry delay
parameters.verbatim: Number 2 delays 2-3 seconds, then maneuvers into the fighting wing cone and calls, "Mistras A2, is in"

parameters.name: general power guide
parameters.value: 85 % in a low area, MAX power in a high area
parameters.verbatim: As a guide, use 85 % in a low area, MAX power in a high area.

parameters.name: Level I parameters (Table 9.4)
parameters.verbatim: 1 I (initial proficiency) Stable Turn 30-60 ~ 2-Gs 50% (fixed)

parameters.name: Level II parameters (Table 9.4)
parameters.value: Turns, Modified Lazy-8, ~120 degrees maximum bank, moderate G, 85 % (low area) / MAX (high area)
parameters.verbatim: 2 II (limited proficiency) Turns, Modified Lazy-8 ~120 Maximum Moderate 85% (low area); MAX (hi area)

parameters.name: Level III parameters (Table 9.4)
parameters.value: Modified Cuban 8, Loop, Cloverleaf, Barrel Roll; bank and G as required; 85 % (low area) / MAX (high area)
parameters.verbatim: 3 III (desired proficiency) Modified Cuban 8, Loop, Cloverleaf, Barrel Roll As required As required 85% (low area); MAX (hi area)

parameters.name: post ET check tolerance
parameters.verbatim: Number 2 responds, "2 same" (if within 50 pounds and 0.5 Gs) or "2.800, 5 Gs". Report the maximum G-reading on all G-checks.

procedure_steps: ET entry: at 180 to 200 KIAS and approximately the middle of the altitude block, Number 1 directs "go extended trail level 1/2"; Number 2 responds; Number 1 makes a moderate G-turn away from Number 2.
Number 2 delays 2-3 seconds, manoeuvres into the fighting wing cone and calls "is in" before Number 1 begins manoeuvring.
Both A/C set and maintain the briefed power setting throughout the exercise.
To transition levels, Number 1 rolls out, levels off and calls the new level; Number 2 acknowledges; set the new power setting after Number 2 acknowledges.
To end the exercise, Number 1 or Number 2 calls "terminate"; Number 1 may reduce power when Number 2 is in sight or acknowledges.
After each ET exercise, Number 1 conducts a fuel and G check using the radio, reporting the maximum G-reading.
common_errors: Abrupt turn reversals by lead are prohibited - turns in one direction followed by a rapid, unanticipated roll in the opposite direction.
Entering the 300-foot bubble (requires "knock it off").
Manoeuvring Over The Top in Level III when Number 1 is blind or Number 2 is not in a position to go Over The Top.
Flying ET with more than two ships - "ET is flown two-ship only."
Continuing a manoeuvre when airspeed, G and AOA are not sufficient.
corrections: If unable to quickly regain the fighting wing cone after a momentary deviation inside 500 feet, call "terminate".
If Number 1 is blind or Number 2 is not in position for Over The Top, maintain Level II until both requirements are satisfied.
If airspeed, G, and AOA are not sufficient to continue a manoeuvre, Terminate or Knock It Off as appropriate.
If Number 2 wants Number 1 to discontinue manoeuvring (for example, loss of spacing), notify Number 1 with a "terminate" call with the reason.
sections.notes: Note under Table 9.4: "Depending on the wingman's proficiency ET Exercise can be initiated from level II or level III."

sections.title: FLYING ET - GENERAL RESPONSIBILITIES
sections.technique_summary: Each pilot is responsible for taking the necessary action to avoid a collision; however, it is Number 2's primary responsibility to avoid hitting Number 1. Because of the dynamic nature of ET, the potential for collision is increased and flying ET requires uncompromising flight discipline. Number 1 is a training platform for Number 2 and must constantly monitor G-loading, remembering that Number 2 typically requires more G than Number 1 to maintain position.

parameters.name: where Number 1 looks for Number 2
parameters.value: behind the wing in the 4-5 o'clock or 7-8 o'clock position
parameters.verbatim: Generally look for Number 2 behind the wing in the 4-5 o'clock or 7-8 o'clock position, and be more vigilant if Number 2 strays from the cone parameters.

procedure_steps: Number 1 constantly monitors Number 2's aspect, range, closure, HCA and LOS for the possibility of an inadvertent 3/9 line or bubble violation.
Number 2 generally uses varying degrees of lead pursuit to maintain the fighting wing cone.

Pause momentarily to see how rapidly Number 1 is moving in the canopy (LOS/LOS rate), predict Number 1's flight path, then manoeuvre by selecting the appropriate pursuit option and lift vector placement.
common_errors: Delaying the KIO call - "Do not delay calling KIO if it is evident one of these situations is about to occur. It is far more desirable to KIO prior to the excursion than to see the situation developing and wait for it to happen."
Number 1 flying tight, high-G manoeuvres that are of little value if Number 2 is unable to maintain proper position.
Number 1 manoeuvring in an unpredictable or abrupt manner that might force Number 2 inside the bubble or forward of the 3/9 line.
Number 2 spending excessive time in lag pursuit - "Normally, little time is spent in lag pursuit."
corrections: If necessary, terminate or transition to the next lower level of ET until Number 2 can establish position in the fighting wing cone.
Use pure and lag pursuit judiciously to avoid high aspect, heading crossing angles and LOS rates.
Use terminate procedures to cease manoeuvring if unable to maintain position.
Any pilot in either A/C must not hesitate to call "Terminate" or "Knock It Off" if appropriate.

sections.title: FLYING ET - LEVEL ONE
sections.technique_summary: Number 1 begins ET Level 1 with a radio call and, after Number 2 acknowledges, enters a moderate G-turn of approximately 2 Gs. Number 2 attempts to use the same power setting as Number 1 to explore and manoeuvre within the fighting wing cone using appropriate pursuit geometry and lift vector placement, learning how difficult it is to stabilize in any one position without the use of power.

parameters.name: G loading
parameters.verbatim: enter a moderate G-turn of approximately 2 Gs

parameters.name: bank and power
parameters.value: 30-60 degrees bank turn with approximately 45-50 % power
parameters.verbatim: Set power to maintain a 30-60 bank turn with approximately 45-50 % power.

procedure_steps: Number 1 calls "go extended trail, Level 1".
After Number 2 acknowledges, Number 1 enters a moderate G-turn of approximately 2 Gs and sets power for a 30-60 degree bank turn with approximately 45-50 % power.
Number 2 uses the same power setting to explore the quadrants of the fighting wing cone using pursuit options and lift vector placement.
sections.notes: Table 9.4 lists 50 % (fixed) power for Level I; the Level 1 narrative gives approximately 45-50 % power.

sections.title: FLYING ET - LEVEL TWO
sections.technique_summary: After Number 2 acknowledges the Level 2 call, Number 1 selects MAX power and turns away from Number 2. Number 2 manoeuvres to the fighting wing cone and calls "is in", then predicts Number 1's flight path and manoeuvres in relation to it, with constant analysis of Number 1's plane of motion and relative aspect, range, closure, HCA and LOS. Pursuit curves exist in both the vertical and horizontal planes.

parameters.name: power for low and medium altitudes
parameters.verbatim: For low and medium altitudes, 85% torque is a good power setting to maintain energy.

parameters.name: power at higher altitudes/temperatures
parameters.verbatim: Higher altitudes and air temperatures or a low initial energy state may require the use of MAX power during maneuvering.

parameters.name: cone to maintain
parameters.value: 30-45 degree cone away from Number 1's high or low 6 o'clock
parameters.verbatim: Attempt to maintain the 30-45 cone away from Number 1's high or low 6 o'clock position.

procedure_steps: Number 1 calls "go extended trail, Level 2"; after Number 2 acknowledges, selects MAX power and turns away from Number 2.
Number 2 manoeuvres to the fighting wing cone and calls "Mistras A2, is in".
Predict Number 1's flight path and manoeuvre in relation to it, analysing plane of motion, aspect, range, closure, HCA and LOS.
Once the desired learning objectives have been met, transition to Level III manoeuvring or terminate.
common_errors: Stagnating in the 5-7 o'clock position - "Transitory periods in Number 1's high or low 6-o'clock position are acceptable; however, avoid stagnating in the 5-7 o'clock position."
Using intentional lag rolls - "Intentional lag rolls are generally not required to maintain the cone."
Over-correcting with exaggerated pursuit curve adjustments held for too long.
corrections: A move toward lag pursuit may generally be the best solution to mitigate these problems; but most of the time, merely using less lead pursuit will adequately solve the problem.
Exaggerated pursuit curve adjustments are normally only required for a short period of time.

sections.title: FLYING ET - LEVEL THREE (INCLUDING OVER THE TOP)
sections.technique_summary: After Number 2 acknowledges the Level 3 call, Number 1 selects MAX power and turns away, and after turning 180 degrees continues straight ahead maintaining 200 KIAS. When Number 2 reports fuel on board, Number 1 rolls into 60 degrees of bank using 2 Gs to maintain level flight and adjusts the PCL to maintain 200 KIAS; when Number 2 calls in, Number 1 uses 85 % torque (low area) or MAX (high area) and starts manoeuvring with hard turns, modified lazy-eights, barrel rolls and Over The Top manoeuvres.

parameters.name: Number 1 setup airspeed
parameters.verbatim: After turning 180 continue straight ahead and maintain 200 KIAS.

parameters.name: Number 1 setup bank and G
parameters.value: 60 degrees of bank, 2 Gs to maintain level flight
parameters.verbatim: roll into 60 of bank, use 2 G's to maintain level flight and adjust the PCL as required to maintain 200 KIAS

parameters.name: manoeuvring power
parameters.verbatim: When No2 reports "Mistras A2, is in" use 85% Torque (low area) or MAX (high area) and start maneuvering.

parameters.name: Number 2 delay after the turn away
parameters.verbatim: wait for 5-8 seconds and then vary bank and back stick pressure to attain 1500 - 2000 foot spacing

parameters.name: Number 2 spacing
parameters.verbatim: attain 1500 - 2000 foot spacing and roll out behind and slightly below Number 1

parameters.name: Number 2 vertical reference
parameters.value: Number 1 approximately 1-2 ship widths above the horizon
parameters.verbatim: Place Number 1 approximately 1-2 ship widths above the horizon.

procedure_steps: Number 1 calls "go Extended Trail, Level 3"; after acknowledgement, selects MAX power and turns away from Number 2, then after 180 degrees continues straight ahead at 200 KIAS.

Number 2 waits 5-8 seconds, varies bank and back stick pressure to attain 1500-2000 foot spacing, rolls out behind and slightly below Number 1 with Number 1 approximately 1-2 ship widths above the horizon, and reports fuel on board.
When Number 1 starts turning, Number 2 uses MAX, Low Yo-Yo, High Yo-Yo and Quarter Plane to manoeuvre to the fighting wing cone and calls "in".
Prioritize between nose track and energy when High AOA, buffet and/or stick shaker indicate the A/C is losing energy.

Apply "lag at the bottom, lead at the top": delay pulling up into the vertical until noticing LOS in the vertical, then at the apex generally sacrifice airspeed for nose track and attempt to beat Number 1's nose through the horizon.
If range and plane are satisfactory, attempt to hit Over The Top with the nose through the horizon before or at the same time as Number 1, with fuselages aligned (zero HCA or angle off).
common_errors: Sacrificing airspeed for nose track without recognizing that it may eventually result in excessive spacing due to airspeed difference, and may place the A/C in a negative energy state.
Relaxing back-stick pressure when Number 1 is in a hard turn - it may preserve energy or increase airspeed but can also result in excessive spacing.
Not recognizing that if Number 1's nose position is below the horizon, the A/C is likely to be accelerating.
Number 1 attempting to force Number 2 to overshoot - "Number 1 will not attempt to force Number 2 to overshoot."
Entering Over The Top manoeuvres without adequate airspeed.
corrections: Conservation of energy is critical during Level 3; manoeuvre in relation to Number 1 and balance the need for nose track or energy through proper pursuit selection and lift vector placement.
Consider Number 2's skill level while manoeuvring to prevent exceeding Number 2's capabilities.
Ensure adequate airspeed is available for over-the-top manoeuvres.
sections.notes: Manoeuvres in ET are not flown with the precise parameters of contact flying; attitudes and airspeeds vary for effective training, area orientation, visual lookout and smoothness.

sections.title: FORMATION RECOVERY - DESCENT TO VFR PATTERN, BREAK AND LANDING
sections.technique_summary: Formation recoveries are similar to single-ship recoveries, but operational restrictions can significantly change recovery options and Number 1 must consider Number 2's capabilities when developing the recovery plan. Once established at pattern altitude inside the entry point, all turns away from Number 2 are echelon unless briefed otherwise. Number 1 positions Number 2 on the side opposite the direction of the Break before North/South Point, turns smoothly to downwind at the Break point and delays power reduction until the turn is initiated.

parameters.name: minimum power in descent
parameters.verbatim: In general, Number 1 should avoid low power settings (less than 20 % torque). Instead of reducing power below 20 % torque, the speed brake may be used.

parameters.name: Number 2 delay after Break
parameters.verbatim: After Number 1 has executed Break, Number 2 waits for a minimum of 5 seconds before starting his turn.

parameters.name: downwind position
parameters.verbatim: On downwind, Number 2 should be slightly outside Number 1's ground track.

parameters.name: landing position
parameters.value: centerline of the runway for both A/C
parameters.verbatim: Number 1 normally lands on the centerline of the runway. Number 2 will land also on the centerline of the runway.

procedure_steps: If weather allows, Number 1 can direct Number 2 to a position (route or fighting wing) that enhances clearing and allows greater manoeuvrability.
Once established at pattern altitude, inside the entry point for the VFR pattern, all turns away from Number 2 are echelon unless briefed otherwise.
Prior to North/South Point, Number 1 positions Number 2 on the side opposite the direction of the Break.
At the Break point, Number 1 smoothly turns to the downwind and delays power reduction until the turn is initiated.
Number 2 waits a minimum of 5 seconds after Number 1's Break before starting the turn and ensures proper spacing on downwind.
Number 2 flies a normal contact pattern; perch point should be the same.
common_errors: Number 1 using low power settings (less than 20 % torque) during the descent.
Number 2 following a poorly-flown pattern - "Number 2 should not follow a poorly-flown pattern. Go-around if required."
Insufficient spacing on downwind.
corrections: Instead of reducing power below 20 % torque, the speed brake may be used.
Go-around if required rather than following a poorly-flown pattern.

sections.title: FORMATION APPROACH
sections.technique_summary: Formation approach procedures are the same as for a single ship. Before starting an instrument penetration, Number 1 positions Number 2 on the side opposite the direction of the penetration turn and on the upwind side of the landing runway. Number 1 directs landing gear and flap configuration with a radio call or visual signal (radio call in IMC), and gear and flaps are normally lowered with only one signal unless briefed otherwise.

parameters.name: minimum torque
parameters.verbatim: Number 1 should not use less than 20% torque.

parameters.name: flap configuration
parameters.verbatim: Formation approaches are flown with flaps in the TO position.

parameters.name: approach airspeed
parameters.verbatim: Maintain 110 KIAS on the instrument approach unless winds dictate otherwise or when a circling approach is planned.

procedure_steps: Before an instrument penetration, position Number 2 on the side opposite the direction of the penetration turn.
Position Number 2 on the upwind side of the landing runway.
Number 1 directs landing gear and flap configuration with a radio call or visual signal (use a radio call in IMC).
Number 2 checks Number 1's A/C configuration and gives a thumbs up; Number 1 checks Number 2 and returns the thumbs up if the configuration looks good.
Number 1 transmits a gear down call for both A/C after configuration is confirmed.
Maintain 110 KIAS on the instrument approach unless winds dictate otherwise or a circling approach is planned.
common_errors: Using less than 20 % torque.
Using visual signals instead of a radio call for configuration changes in IMC.

sections.title: FORMATION GO-AROUND
sections.technique_summary: For a formation go-around, Number 1 smoothly adds power to approximately 75 % torque and follows normal formation takeoff and single ship go-around procedures. If splitting in the pattern after a formation go-around or low approach, the A/C on the inside of the pattern pulls for a closed pattern or turns crosswind first.

parameters.name: go-around power
parameters.verbatim: Number 1 smoothly adds power to approximately 75% torque, follows normal formation takeoff, and single ship go-around procedures.

procedure_steps: Number 1 smoothly adds power to approximately 75 % torque.
Follow normal formation takeoff and single ship go-around procedures.
If splitting in the pattern, the A/C on the inside of the pattern pulls for a closed pattern or turns crosswind first.
corrections: Number 1 should have positioned Number 2 on the upwind side of the landing runway.

sections.title: FORMATION MISSED APPROACH
sections.technique_summary: The potential for lost wingman and for spatial disorientation is high during a formation missed approach. Smoothly advance power to approximately 75 %, as in the formation go-around, and slowly and smoothly establish the missed approach pitch attitude. Use the radio to direct gear and flap retraction and ensure the minimum climb gradient is maintained.

parameters.name: missed approach power
parameters.verbatim: Smoothly advance power to approximately 75 %, as in the formation Go-Around

procedure_steps: Smoothly advance power to approximately 75 %.
Slowly and smoothly establish the missed approach pitch attitude.
Use the radio to direct gear and flap retraction.
Ensure the minimum climb gradient is maintained.
common_errors: High potential for lost wingman and for spatial disorientation.
corrections: A/C attitude calls to Number 2 can help avoid spatial disorientation.
sections.notes: Figure 9.31 (Stacked level on Final) accompanies this paragraph.

sections.title: FORMATION TAKEOFF ABNORMALITIES AND ABORTS
sections.technique_summary: If Number 2 overruns Number 1, Number 2 selects MAX power and makes a separate takeoff while maintaining the same side of the runway and follows Number 1's directions. If Number 2 falls behind, Number 2 crosschecks engine instruments and airspeed and aborts (if there is a problem) or performs a separate takeoff, rejoining after becoming safely airborne. During an abort, maintain A/C control, ensure separation from the other A/C by maintaining the respective side of the runway, and make a radio call as soon as practical.

parameters.name: element abort call
parameters.value: "abort, abort, abort" with the word flight
parameters.verbatim: Number 1 directs an element abort with a radio call, "Mistras A abort, abort, abort." The operative word flight indicates both A/C should abort.

parameters.name: interval takeoff abort at Kalamata
parameters.value: Number 2 is always below abort speed at Kalamata airport
parameters.verbatim: If Number 2 is rolling, but below abort speed (generally in Kalamata airport Number 2 is always below abort speed), an abort must also be executed.

procedure_steps: Number 2 passing Number 1: select MAX power and make a separate takeoff while maintaining the same side of the runway; follow Number 1's directions.
Number 2 falling behind: crosscheck engine instruments and airspeed indicator, then abort (if there is a problem) or perform a separate takeoff and rejoin after becoming safely airborne.

Formation takeoff abort (one A/C): maintain A/C control, maintain the respective side of the runway, make a radio call as soon as practical; the A/C continuing advances PCL to MAX power, maintains its side of the runway and executes a normal single-ship takeoff.

Interval takeoff abort: if Number 1 aborts, transmit a radio call when practical; if Number 2 has not released brakes, reduce power to idle and hold position until Number 1 clears the runway; if rolling but below abort speed, abort; if above abort speed, continue the takeoff.
Element abort: each A/C maintains its respective side of the runway and makes every effort to stop prior to the end of the runway.
common_errors: Sympathetic aborts after brake release during a formation takeoff - "there are normally no sympathetic aborts after brake release. Sympathetic aborts can create situations in which the good A/C risks making the situation worse by adding another A/C into the high-speed abort situation; risk of collision, hot brakes, or blown tires increases."
Sacrificing A/C control to make a radio call - "Do not sacrifice A/C control to make a radio call."
Difficulty for Number 2 to recognize an abort using only visual cues during an interval takeoff.
corrections: Maintain A/C control and ensure separation from the other A/C by maintaining the respective side of the runway.

sections.title: AIRBORNE EMERGENCIES (GENERAL)
sections.technique_summary: Maintain formation integrity to the maximum extent possible during airborne emergencies; mutual support is one of the primary reasons for formation flying. If either member must return to the airfield due to an emergency, the other A/C should also return and provide assistance. In general, the A/C with a malfunction should be given the Number 1 position so it can handle the emergency without maintaining formation position.

parameters.name: Number 1 position offers
parameters.verbatim: The Number 1 position should be offered three times: a. When the emergency occurs, b. When on recovery when below the weather and able to navigate VFR to the field, c. When on final with the field in sight.

parameters.name: minimum spacing with an emergency
parameters.verbatim: Except in IMC, avoid flying closer than route formation as Number 2.

procedure_steps: The formation member having the emergency notifies the other members about the problem, his intentions, and the type of assistance required.
If an A/C malfunction occurs while in fingertip, increase A/C separation before handling the emergency, if weather permits.
In VMC without engine problems, the A/C having the emergency generally leads back to a Straight In; in IMC, it generally leads back to an instrument approach.
Number 2: when a malfunction is encountered, call Knock It Off and inform Number 1 of the problem; normally take the Number 1 position when offered, if able to communicate and navigate.
common_errors: Flying in the Number 2 position with an emergency - "Generally, avoid flying in Number 2 position with an emergency."
Flying closer than route spacing while carrying an emergency (except in IMC).
corrections: If Number 2 refuses the Number 1 position at any time, offer it at each successive point as described.
If Number 2 is able to communicate over the radio, Number 1 should offer verbal assistance as necessary.
Follow the preflight briefing instructions for emergencies as much as practical.

sections.title: ENGINE PROBLEMS, PHYSIOLOGICAL INCIDENT, BIRD STRIKE, MIDAIR COLLISION
sections.technique_summary: With engine problems the emergency A/C leads back to execute a PEL; if weather or field conditions at the intended recovery runway are unknown, the other formation member may be sent ahead to report on airfield conditions. For a physiological incident the A/C having the emergency typically leads back. If a bird strike appears imminent, do not attempt evasive manoeuvres into the other A/C. If a midair collision occurs between formation members, they shall not act as chase ships for each other.
procedure_steps: Engine problems: the emergency A/C leads back to execute a PEL; the other member may be sent ahead to report airfield conditions and radio back.
Physiological incident: the A/C having the emergency typically leads back; the other member uses caution and sound judgment, especially if penetration during IMC is required.
Bird strike: the primary concern is to avoid midair collision and A/C separation; if a strike occurs, ensure A/C separation before handling the emergency.
Midair collision: Number 1 should coordinate separate clearances and chase ships.
common_errors: Attempting evasive manoeuvres into the other A/C in an effort to avoid a bird.
Formation members acting as chase ships for each other after a midair collision - "they shall not act as chase ships for each other."
corrections: Consider executing a crab landing if forward visibility is severely restricted after a bird strike.

sections.title: SPATIAL DISORIENTATION IN FORMATION
sections.technique_summary: If either pilot suffers spatial disorientation, immediately inform the other A/C and transfer A/C control to the other pilot if practical. If Number 2 is disoriented, the PNF in the Number 1 A/C advises Number 2 of A/C attitude, altitude, heading and airspeed; if symptoms persist and conditions permit, Number 1 should establish straight and level flight for 30 to 60 seconds and, if possible, get the formation to VMC conditions.

parameters.name: straight and level relief period
parameters.verbatim: If symptoms persist and conditions permit, Number 1 should establish Straight And Level flight for 30 to 60 seconds.

procedure_steps: Number 1 disoriented: immediately inform Number 2 and transfer A/C control to the other pilot if practical; if transfer is not an option, confirm attitude with the other crewmember or Number 2; if symptoms persist, terminate the mission and recover by the simplest and safest route possible.
Number 2 disoriented: immediately inform Number 1 and transfer A/C control to the other pilot if practical; the PNF in Number 1 advises Number 2 of attitude, altitude, heading and airspeed.
If symptoms persist and conditions permit, Number 1 establishes straight and level flight for 30 to 60 seconds and, if possible, gets the formation to VMC.
If the problem persists, consider offering the Number 1 position.
common_errors: Initiating lost wingman procedures while disoriented - "As Number 2, be cautious when initiating lost wingman procedures as this could trigger further spatial disorientation."
corrections: If unable to maintain position, and Number 2 becomes a threat to Number 1, a breakout should be initiated.
If necessary, terminate the mission and recover by the simplest and safest route possible.

sections.title: A/C STROBE LIGHTS AND ICING
sections.technique_summary: Number 1's strobe lights may distract Number 2 and could lead to spatial disorientation; Number 2 should advise Number 1 if the strobes create a problem and Number 1 should turn them off. If the Number 2 A/C experiences icing, Number 2 notifies Number 1, who should climb or descend to avoid continuous cruising in icing conditions.
procedure_steps: Number 2 advises Number 1 if the strobes create a problem; Number 1 turns them off.
If Number 2 experiences icing, notify Number 1; Number 1 climbs or descends to avoid continuous cruising in icing conditions.

sections.title: NO RADIO (NORDO)
sections.technique_summary: When a member of the formation has a total radio failure, the NORDO A/C normally receives or retains the Number 2 position. The flight member with the operative radio leads the NORDO A/C into the overhead pattern, notifies the tower and plans for a low approach to the active runway; the NORDO A/C flies a normal pattern and landing. When Number 1 clears Number 2's landing with ATC, Number 1 informs Number 2 by a visual signal and Number 2 assumes landing clearance and lands normally.

parameters.name: NORDO rejoin limit
parameters.value: no closer than route position until directed
parameters.verbatim: the NORDO A/C should cautiously attempt to rejoin (no closer than route). Rock wings (attention in the air) and move no closer than route position until directed.

procedure_steps: The A/C with the operative radio leads the NORDO A/C into the overhead pattern, notifies the tower, and plans for a low approach to the active runway.
If weather prevents an overhead pattern, execute a Straight In or instrument approach as appropriate.
With a total radio failure while in fingertip, Number 2 manoeuvres to route, attracts the attention of Number 1, and shows the appropriate visual signal.
If in other than fingertip or route position and a rejoin is not anticipated, the NORDO A/C cautiously attempts to rejoin no closer than route, rocking wings (attention in the air) until directed.
Terminate the mission as soon as practical and lead the NORDO A/C to the base of intended landing.
common_errors: Rejoining closer than route position before being directed.

sections.title: EJECTION
sections.technique_summary: If ejection is required, Number 2 acts as the On Scene Commander (rescue combat air patrol [RESCAP] commander) until relieved or bingo fuel is reached.

parameters.name: duration of On Scene Commander duty
parameters.value: until relieved or bingo fuel is reached
parameters.verbatim: Number 2 acts as the On Scene Commander (rescue combat air patrol [RESCAP] commander) until relieved or bingo fuel is reached.

procedure_steps: Number 2 acts as the On Scene Commander (RESCAP commander) until relieved or bingo fuel is reached.
sections.notes: Local in-flight guides will outline local specifics.
